title: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
shortDescription: A misfire has been detected on cylinder 1.
fullDescription: The PCM has detected that combustion in cylinder 1 is incomplete or absent for a number of crankshaft events that exceeds the misfire threshold. Damage to the catalytic converter can occur if the condition persists.
safetyImpact: Severe misfires can cause sudden power loss in traffic and rapid catalytic converter damage; resolve promptly.

causes.cause: Worn, fouled, or incorrect-gap spark plugs
Failed ignition coil, coil pack, or coil-on-plug boot
Clogged or leaking fuel injector on the affected cylinder
Loss of compression — burnt valve, worn rings, or head gasket
Vacuum leak at intake manifold or PCV system
Failed knock sensor, crank sensor, or wiring chafe

symptoms: Check Engine Light flashing during active misfire
Rough idle and engine vibration
Loss of power or hesitation under load
Smell of unburned fuel from the exhaust
Decreased fuel economy and possible catalyst damage

fixSteps.title: Confirm misfire location
fixSteps.instruction: Read freeze frame and misfire counters per cylinder. Note which cylinder(s) have the highest counts and the engine load/RPM where the misfire occurred.

fixSteps.title: Swap ignition components
fixSteps.instruction: Move the spark plug and ignition coil from the affected cylinder to a known-good cylinder. Clear codes and re-test — if the misfire moves, the swapped component is the cause.

fixSteps.title: Test fuel injector and compression
fixSteps.instruction: Listen for injector click or use a noid light. Perform a compression test on the affected cylinder and compare to neighboring cylinders. Significantly low compression points to mechanical damage.

fixSteps.title: Inspect crank/knock sensor wiring
fixSteps.instruction: For knock or crank-related codes (P0324–P0335), inspect harness routing for chafe near hot exhaust components. Verify resistance against OEM spec and torque sensor mounting bolt to specification.

faq.q: Why is my Check Engine Light flashing?
faq.a: A flashing CEL means the misfire is severe enough to damage the catalytic converter. Reduce load, get off the highway, and address it before continuing to drive.

faq.q: Can bad fuel cause a misfire?
faq.a: Yes — water, ethanol issues, or extremely low octane can all cause misfire DTCs. Try a tank of high-quality fuel after addressing any underlying mechanical issues.

faq.q: Are knock sensor codes urgent?
faq.a: If a knock sensor is faulty, the PCM typically retards timing as a protective measure, leading to power loss and worse fuel economy but not immediate damage. Repair within a few hundred miles.
